writeup.p: Join-time world metadata: the server announces its difficulty once, inside ServerConfigurationManager.initializeConnectionToPlayer, alongside the other world-state packets (S05 spawn position, S03 time of day, S44 world border INITIALIZE). The payload is a single unsigned byte 0-3 mapped to EnumDifficulty. Vanilla never re-broadcasts it: the /difficulty command mutates the server WorldInfo without notifying clients, so the value learned at join stays stale for the whole session.

The client handler handleServerDifficulty writes the value into WorldInfo (setDifficulty and setDifficultyLocked) and nothing else; gameplay code reads it later via world.getDifficulty(). Note the asymmetry: the packet has a difficultyLocked constructor field and getter, but neither readPacketData nor writePacketData ever touches it, so the wire format is one byte and the locked flag is permanently false on the client.

None of the 8 clients contains a module that references S41. The only non-vanilla hits are Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 NetworkAPI.java, which registers the class in the list of packet types exposed to the JavaScript scripting bridge; no shipped script uses it. The reason is functional: difficulty only scales vanilla survival math (mob damage, hunger drain, regeneration), and cheat modules replace that math with their own logic, so no module output depends on the server's difficulty setting.

The value is trust-on-receive. readPacketData feeds the raw byte to EnumDifficulty.getDifficultyEnum, which in 1.8.9 clamps with a modulo (difficultyEnums[p % 4]), so out-of-range bytes wrap instead of crashing: 4 maps to peaceful, 5 to easy, and so on. The handler stores the enum without validation. That is the entire surface: a hostile server can only lie about difficulty, which changes nothing a client-side cheat relies on.

overview: One-byte join-time announcement of the world difficulty, written straight into WorldInfo by the client handler. In the 8 clients it is invisible: no module references it, the locked flag is dead on the wire, and out-of-range bytes wrap modulo 4. The only non-vanilla trace is Rise's script API registering the class for JS packet filtering.
server_handling: ServerConfigurationManager.initializeConnectionToPlayer sends new S41PacketServerDifficulty(worldinfo.getDifficulty(), worldinfo.isDifficultyLocked()) (line 136 in the Rise 6.x bundled sources, 163 in the MCP builds). It is sent exactly once per join, before the initial S08 teleport completes the login sequence. Nothing else on the vanilla server constructs the packet; /difficulty changes WorldInfo directly and does not broadcast.
protocol_notes: Wire format in 1.8.9 is a single unsigned byte (writeByte / readUnsignedByte) despite the packet metadata table listing a difficultyLocked boolean. The boolean exists as a constructor argument and getter but is never serialized, so clients always see difficultyLocked == false. EnumDifficulty.getDifficultyEnum applies difficultyEnums[p % 4], so any byte value is accepted. Play state only; sent once during join before the player is fully active.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures this packet. It is clientbound, unidirectional, sent once, and carries no timing or state information that movement or combat checks could use. Spoofing or cancelling it would only change the client's local mob-damage math, which is irrelevant to server-side validation.
